subject: Transportation Systems
title: The Panama Canal
description: A quick win: understand The Panama Canal.

hook.text: The Panama Canal lets ships cross from the Atlantic to the Pacific without rounding South America.

buildup.text: Building it took 10 years and killed over 5,000 workers—mostly from malaria and yellow fever.

discovery.text: Ships enter locks that lift them 85 feet above sea level to cross a man-made lake, then lower them again.

twist.text: The original locks limited ship size for a century. A 2016 expansion doubled the canal's capacity.

climax.text: New Panamax ships are designed specifically to fit the expanded locks—every inch counts.

punchline.text: Locks lift ships over a continent.

quiz.question: How does the Panama Canal move ships between oceans?
options: Locks lift ships 85 feet to cross a lake, then lower them
